$doc: Candidate serving configuration. The `overrides` block is the vLLM surface (vLLM tracks only): the trusted GB10 runner fetches it at your submitted commit, validates it against a strict whitelist, deploys it as the candidate engine, and measures it paired against the pinned baseline. Empty overrides reproduce the baseline. Allowed keys: kernels (bool, loads Sources/kernels), vllmSource (bool, applies Sources/vllm-patches), maxNumSeqs (1-8), maxNumBatchedTokens (512-16384), enforceEager (bool), compilationLevel (0-3), speculative ({model: pinned Poolside DFlash NVFP4 id, numSpeculativeTokens: 1-15}). attentionBackend is DISABLED: all three previously-whitelisted values were measured diverging from the pinned batch-invariant baseline. Greedy output must survive your configuration: teacher-forced agreement below 90% is rejected.
$doc_speculative: The top-level `speculative` block is the llama.cpp surface, read by the trusted llama.cpp runners. It appends `--spec-type` (and, for types that need a draft model, the draft the runner has pinned for the track) to the otherwise fixed llama-server command. Fields: specType (one of the values the pinned build parses), draftMax and draftMin (1-16). Note that draftMax and draftMin are inert for the ngram-* types, which take their own width from their size_m; they are omitted here rather than set to a value that never reaches the engine.
